## FAO HITL Sweeper v1

**Controls:** FAO-GOV-004, FAO-GOV-007, FAO-GOV-008

Every 5 minutes, **Run Sweep** calls `fao_maintenance_sweep`. In the database it expires unclaimed run tokens, fails stale runs, expires overdue requests (HITL_EXPIRED is the expiry record, followed by the escalation; no COMMITTED row, COMMIT_BLOCKED only when the audit chain is incomplete), writes escalation events, and lists the notifications that are due.

- **Expand Notifications** turns the escalation and re-notify lists into notifier inputs; the notifier runs once per item and one failure does not stop the others
- **Check Notifier Results** runs after every item was attempted and lists each failed notifier call; it does not stop the execution
- **Check Sweep Errors** sits below Expand Notifications, so with execution order v1 it runs last, on every sweep. It fails the execution once, naming both the notifier failures (FAO-GOV-007) and the sweep item errors (FAO-GOV-008), and fails closed when notices were listed but no notifier results can be read

Deadlines do not depend on this schedule: `fao_hitl_decide` refuses a decision at or after the deadline on its own.

A failed sweep (Run Sweep or Check Sweep Errors) reaches `fao_error_handler_v1` (`errorWorkflow`), which records one `workflow_failures` row with source `sweeper`.

**Publish (n8n 2.x):** step 4 of 5 (Writer, error handler, notifier, sweeper, flagship). Publish after the error handler and the notifier; its schedule starts sweeping as soon as it is published.
